claim: For every positive integer \(n\), the congruence \(T_aT_b+n\equiv c^2\pmod M\), with \(T_j=j(j+1)/2\), has integer solutions \((a,b,c)\) for every positive modulus \(M\) if and only if \(n\not\equiv2,5\pmod 9\).
integrity: The proof is self-contained apart from standard Hensel lifting and the Chinese remainder theorem; literature comparisons distinguish local congruence solvability from actual integral-pair existence.
scientific_limitations: This is a local congruence-solvability theorem. It does not imply an integral triangular D(n)-pair for admissible n, and finite verifier output is corroborative rather than a proof of the universal statement.
title: Exact congruence obstruction for triangular \(D(n)\) pairs
